Office of the City Historian of Havana (state budget and other authorised sources, per Decree-Law 368 of 2018).
Under the Office of the City Historian of Havana, which also runs the adjoining Templete.

n: Gran Teatro de La Habana Alicia Alonso
f: State theatre run by the Consejo Nacional de las Artes Escénicas, under the Ministry of Culture. Reopened in 2016 after a three-year restoration; new repairs were under way in 2025.
w: Home of the Ballet Nacional de Cuba. The council's president named roof, air-conditioning and vibration damage behind the 2025 repair.
x: The council's president explained the 2025 repair on Canal Habana's magazine programme; no accounts or funder list is public.
Ministry of Culture (state budget), through the Consejo Nacional de las Artes Escénicas; ticket sales.
Run by the Consejo Nacional de las Artes Escénicas, which also runs the Teatro Nacional de Cuba. Home of the Ballet Nacional de Cuba and the Teatro Lírico Nacional's opera seasons.

f: Founded in 1948 by Alicia Alonso and paid by the Cuban state. The British Friends of Ballet Nacional de Cuba, a UK charity, exist to fund equipment and new productions.
w: Down to 55 dancers in 2025 from over 100 at times, as members took jobs abroad (New York Times).
x: The British Friends file public accounts with the Charity Commission (income £8,150 in the year to 31 December 2025).
Cuban state budget; British Friends of Ballet Nacional de Cuba, a UK charity (income £8,150 in 2025), for equipment and new productions.
Resident at the Gran Teatro de La Habana Alicia Alonso. Its official school is the Cuban National Ballet School.

f: State theatre run by the Consejo Nacional de las Artes Escénicas under the Ministry of Culture. Built from 1951 and opened in 1979; its two halls seat 2,254 and 805.
w: Its Sala Avellaneda hosted the opening concert of the 41st Jazz Plaza festival in January 2026.
x: EcuRed lists the theatre among the council's institutions; no accounts or funder list is public.
Ministry of Culture (state budget), through the Consejo Nacional de las Artes Escénicas.
Part of the Consejo Nacional de las Artes Escénicas, with the Gran Teatro de La Habana Alicia Alonso and the Teatro Julio Antonio Mella.

f: Film archive and cinema programme created in 1960 as a department of ICAIC, which sits in the Ministry of Culture. It moved into Alfredo Guevara's former house in October 2020.
w: Member of the International Federation of Film Archives (FIAF). ICAIC, its parent, carries the censorship and protest flags.
x: The archive's site posts screening programmes by date range and a chronology of its history; no accounts or funder list is public.
Ministry of Culture (state budget), through ICAIC.
Department of ICAIC. Member of the International Federation of Film Archives (FIAF).

n: Instituto Cubano del Arte e Industria Cinematográficos (ICAIC)
f: State film body created by Law No. 169 in 1959, funded through the Ministry of Culture. It runs the Cinemateca, the Havana film festival, the Muestra Joven and animation studios.
w: Flags: State censorship or punishment, Protest or boycott. Films pulled: Regreso a Ítaca 2014, Santa y Andrés 2016, Sueños al pairo 2020. Twelve filmmakers protested in 2014; others withdrew works in 2020.
x: ICAIC's Cubacine site carries the quarterly magazine Cine Cubano, the monthly paper Cartelera Cine y Video and calls for its Fondo de Fomento del Cine Cubano; no accounts or funder list is public.
Part of the Ministry of Culture system. Runs the Cinemateca de Cuba, the Havana film festival, the Muestra Joven, animation studios and the national film distributor.

n: Festival Internacional del Nuevo Cine Latinoamericano de La Habana
f: Annual December festival organised by ICAIC, a Ministry of Culture body, since 1979. Its founder Alfredo Guevara chaired it until his death in 2013.
w: Flags: State censorship or punishment, Protest or boycott. The festival dropped Regreso a Ítaca in 2014 on ministry and ICAIC orders, said twelve filmmakers who protested. ICAIC dropped Santa y Andrés in 2016.
x: Each year it opens a call for entries and announces its Premios Corales.
Ministry of Culture (state budget), through ICAIC.
Organised by ICAIC, which also runs the Cinemateca de Cuba and the Muestra Joven.

n: Universidad de las Artes de Cuba (ISA)
f: State university in the Ministry of Culture system. Italy agreed in February 2019 to give 2.5 million euros to renovate the theatre faculty and fund teaching and events.
w: Its theatre faculty building is a national monument; the National Art Schools complex was on the World Monuments Fund watch list in 2000 and 2016.
x: The university's site lists its structure, authorities and a repository; no accounts or funder list is public.

Ministry of Culture (state budget); Italy's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, 2.5 million euros agreed in February 2019 for the theatre faculty and the university's activities.
Coordinates the Red Universitaria de las Artes, about thirty arts universities in the Americas, Europe and Africa. Founded in 1976 as the Instituto Superior de Arte.

n: Unión de Escritores y Artistas de Cuba (UNEAC)
f: Membership union founded in 1961 that runs galleries, magazines and the Premios Caracol, given since 1978. Its 2020 statutes list dues, a state contribution and donations as income.
w: Flags: State censorship or punishment. UNEAC expelled historian Alina Bárbara López on 12 September 2024, citing criticism of Revolution leaders, 11 July solidarity and offence to a Party official (14ymedio).
x: UNEAC's site posts its 2020 statutes, which name its income sources and give no amounts.
Member dues; a state contribution, donations, bequests and other income, per article 81 of its 2020 statutes.

Five national associations (performing artists, visual artists, writers, musicians, and film, radio and television makers) and 14 provincial committees. The Premios Caracol cover film, radio, television and criticism.

n: Biblioteca Nacional de Cuba José Martí
f: State library in the Ministry of Culture system and head of the national public library network. Declared a National Monument on 30 June 2021.
w: Contributes digitised material to the Digital Library of the Caribbean, which holds a Celebrating Cuba collection built with other partners.
x: The library's site lists catalogues and its magazines Bibliotecas and Librínsula; no accounts or funder list is public.
Heads the Sistema Nacional de Bibliotecas Públicas Cubanas. Partner in the Digital Library of the Caribbean.

n: Feria Internacional del Libro de La Habana
f: Book fair held since 1982, annual since 2000, run by the Instituto Cubano del Libro, a Ministry of Culture body. The 34th edition opened in August 2026 after a postponement.
w: The 34th edition honoured the centenary of Fidel Castro's birth, had Russia as guest country and moved to Línea y 18 from La Cabaña.
x: The Instituto Cubano del Libro announces dates, guest country and programme; no budget or funder list is public.
Ministry of Culture (state budget), through the Instituto Cubano del Libro.
Run by the Instituto Cubano del Libro, in the Ministry of Culture system. Tours the provinces after Havana, as it has since 2002.

f: State record company founded in 1964, in the Ministry of Culture system. Sony Music has distributed its albums abroad since 2015; Sony/ATV has licensed its songs since January 2018.
w: A 2017 study by Cuba's music research centre, cited by Wikipedia, gave EGREM 58 percent of Cuban digital music revenue in 2016.
x: Sony/ATV said it takes a standard commission on EGREM licensing and declined to give other terms of the 2018 deal (AP).
Cuban state (Ministry of Culture); income from recordings, publishing and physical record sales. Sony/ATV takes a standard commission on licensing.
State music company in the Ministry of Culture system. Runs the Areíto studios, Casas de la Música in six cities and the Musicuba and Son de Cuba artist agencies.

f: Annual January jazz festival first held in 1980 and organised by the Instituto Cubano de la Música. The 42nd edition is set for 24 to 31 January 2027.
w: Holguín was announced as a venue for the 41st edition (Prensa Latina, November 2025). Organisers say over 120 US artists have confirmed for 2027.
x: Each year organisers present a poster, spot and theme song at a press conference; no accounts or sponsor list is public.
Ministry of Culture (state budget), through the Instituto Cubano de la Música.
Organised by the Instituto Cubano de la Música, part of the Ministry of Culture system. The 41st edition used the Sala Avellaneda of the Teatro Nacional de Cuba, per EcuRed.

f: Screening of young Cuban directors' films run by ICAIC with a filmmakers' board. The 19th edition, set for April 2020, was postponed; 14ymedio wrote in 2025 that it had disappeared.
w: Flags: State censorship or punishment, Protest or boycott. 2018: ICAIC moved one film to a 24-seat room; the director withdrew it. 2020: ICAIC cut a documentary and at least six filmmakers withdrew works.
x: The Muestra's site publishes each edition's competition list, awards and poster contest; no accounts or sponsor list is public.
Ministry of Culture (state budget), through ICAIC. In 2019 collateral awards came from the EICTV, the Asociación Hermanos Saíz, SIGNIS Cuba and other Cuban bodies.
Run by ICAIC, which also runs the Cinemateca de Cuba and the Havana film festival.

n: Escuela Internacional de Cine y Televisión (EICTV)
c: San Antonio de los Baños, Cuba
f: The Cuban government supported it at founding. Tuition was 5,000 euros a year in 2011 (AFP). EU-financed UNESCO Transcultura supplied equipment and courses valued at 600,000 euros in 2024.
w: The school's site lists the Ministry of Culture and ICAIC as supporters. In 2026 it also runs a donation campaign for energy autonomy.
x: The school's site lists workshops, news and a donation campaign; no accounts or donor list is public.

Student tuition and workshop fees. Its site lists the Fundación del Nuevo Cine Latinoamericano, the Ministry of Culture and ICAIC as supporters, and Ibermedia, UNESCO and RTVE as collaborators. The EU financed the UNESCO Transcultura programme that supplied equipment in 2024.

Branch of the Fundación del Nuevo Cine Latinoamericano, set up in 1986 by García Márquez, Birri and García Espinosa. Member of CILECT, the international association of film schools, and founding member of FEISAL.

f: Founded in 1899 by Santiago's mayor Emilio Bacardí, this state museum got its building in 1927 from his widow Elvira Cape. The Ministry of Culture's provincial heritage centre oversees it.
w: National Monument since 1999. OnCuba reports more than 23,000 items in three halls and an art annex.
x: Ministry of Culture heritage system (Cuban state), through the Centro Provincial de Patrimonio Cultural de Santiago de Cuba. Elvira Cape, widow of founder Emilio Bacardí, donated the building in 1927.

A provincial museum held by the Centro Provincial de Patrimonio Cultural de Santiago de Cuba, in the Consejo Nacional de Patrimonio Cultural system (Ministry of Culture). Runs the Sala de Arte Extensión annex in the former Club San Carlos.

n: Museo Castillo del Morro San Pedro de la Roca
f: Cuban state property; UNESCO names the Consejo Nacional del Patrimonio Cultural as responsible agency. A museum opened in the fortress on 23 July 1978. State bodies began repairs in 2020.
w: UNESCO World Heritage site since 1997. Granma, quoted by OnCuba in April 2021, reported the repairs would continue through 2021.
x: UNESCO's listing text names the owner and the responsible national agency.

Cuban state (Ministry of Culture) through the Consejo Nacional de Patrimonio Cultural. The Oficina del Conservador, the Centro Provincial de Patrimonio Cultural and the Empresa de Restauración y Conservación de Monumentos began repairs in 2020 (Granma via OnCuba).

UNESCO names the Consejo Nacional del Patrimonio Cultural (Ministry of Culture) as the responsible national agency. The Centro Provincial de Patrimonio Cultural de Santiago de Cuba took part in the 2020 to 2021 repairs (Granma via OnCuba).

f: Private studio-gallery founded in Havana in 1995 by curator Cristina Vives and photographer José A. Figueroa. It describes itself as self-financed; the Norwegian Embassy in Cuba is a named collaborator.
w: Founders say the private studio has no legal support and faces hostility. Dialogue with state institutions has been on and off and one-way (IPS, 2020).
x: Its site lists exhibitions, artists, publications and the studio's history; it carries no accounts, funder list or board.
Self-financed by the Figueroa-Vives family, by its own account. The founders call the Norwegian Embassy in Cuba a collaborator and say international ties are synergy, not grants.
Independent, with no parent body. Its curators belong to UNEAC, CIMAM and AICA; Cristina Figueroa also curates for Casa de las Américas.

f: Open as a museum since 1974, the Palacio Brunet is an 1808 mansion restored from 1964. The Sancti Spíritus heritage centre's 2024 summer programme includes this state museum.
w: The Asociación Pro Trinidad bought the palace in 1945. Trinidad's historic centre has been on the UNESCO list since 1988.
x: Ministry of Culture heritage bodies (Cuban state): the Sancti Spíritus Centro Provincial de Patrimonio and the Consejo Nacional de Patrimonio Cultural.

One of the museums around Trinidad's Plaza Mayor, inside the UNESCO-listed historic centre. Named in the Sancti Spíritus Centro Provincial de Patrimonio's 2024 summer programme (Prensa Latina). Won the 2024 Museo del Año prize from ICOM's Cuban committee and the Consejo Nacional de Patrimonio Cultural.

f: Opened in 1955 in a former cavalry barracks, Camagüey's provincial museum is a state institution. A private Patronato Pro Museo assembled its first collection.
w: Holds Cuban painting including Wifredo Lam and Amelia Peláez, plus natural history and decorative arts rooms.
x: Camagüey's Dirección Provincial de Cultura portal describes the museum, its halls and weekly activities; it links no accounts.
Camagüey's Dirección Provincial de Cultura and Centro Provincial de Patrimonio Cultural, both within the Ministry of Culture (Cuban state).

Listed among the museums on the official page of the Dirección Provincial de Cultura de Camagüey (portal, 2022). The Centro Provincial de Patrimonio Cultural's director spoke for the capital's museums, this one included (ACN via OnCuba, June 2020).

f: State theatre in Cienfuegos, a National Monument. Built 1887 to 1890 with 115,000 gold pesos set aside by the heirs of slave-owning sugar planter Tomás Terry.
w: The building won the National Conservation Prize in 2008. Spanish Wikipedia lists it among eight large colonial-era theatres.
x: The Azurina culture portal lists its director, address and hours; it links no accounts.
Cienfuegos culture sector (Cuban state). Founding capital of 115,000 gold pesos came from the Sucesión de Don Tomás Terry, a civil society of the Terry heirs (EcuRed).

Listed with its director, Miguel Cañellas Sueiras, in the Azurina culture portal's directory of Cienfuegos institutions (2021). Grouped with the Sauto in Matanzas among the eight large colonial-era theatres (Spanish Wikipedia).

f: Matanzas state theatre, a National Monument since 1978, closed 2010 to 2018 for restoration (EcuRed: 2019). Its main hall closed mid-2024; ACN said in July 2025 it would reopen.
w: The state heritage council gave the restoration its 2020 National Restoration Prize. Seating is 775.
x: Ministry of Culture system (Cuban state). The Matanzas Dirección Provincial de Cultura speaks for its programme (ACN via Girón, 2022); the Consejo Nacional de Patrimonio Cultural gave the 2020 restoration prize.

Sub-venue of Cuba's International Ballet Festival and the Mayo Teatral (English Wikipedia). Its director consulted the Consejo Nacional de Patrimonio on the 2024 to 2025 ceiling repair (ACN via Girón, 12 July 2025). Grouped with the Terry in Cienfuegos among the eight large colonial-era theatres.

c: San Antonio de los Baños, Cuba
f: Opened 17 March 1979 per EcuRed (14ymedio: 1948) in an 1830 house in San Antonio de los Baños; the Ministry of Culture is its parent body, per EcuRed.
w: Hosts the Bienal Internacional del Humor, whose 24th edition ran in April 2025 (Cubaperiodistas). EcuRed counts over 10,000 works from 40 countries.
x: Ministry of Culture, the parent body named by EcuRed. The Artemisa Dirección Provincial de Cultura co-sponsors the Bienal, which the Unión de Periodistas de Cuba organises with the museum (OnCuba, 2023).
Parent body: Ministry of Culture. Organises the Bienal Internacional del Humor with the Unión de Periodistas de Cuba, and hosts the Juan David caricature and Humoranga Ariguanabense salons.

n: American Museum of the Cuban Diaspora
f: Non-profit Cuban Museum Inc. A $10 million Miami-Dade County bond grant (2004) built it and county funds support it. The City of Miami added $175,000 in American Rescue Plan money.
w: In September 2017 seven of 13 county commissioners moved $550,000 from the Pérez Art Museum to this museum; Jorge Pérez called it punishment.
x: Files a full Form 990 (2024 on ProPublica) and lists its board on its site.
2024 revenue $933,495: contributions $843,989, program services $89,506; expenses $1,142,164 (Form 990 of Cuban Museum Inc, ProPublica).

Miami-Dade County: a $10 million bond grant (2004) and Department of Cultural Affairs operating support, a third of the 2018 operating budget by its spokeswoman's account. City of Miami: $175,000 in American Rescue Plan money (resolution R-23-0114). Contributions: $843,989 of 2024 revenue.
Operated by the non-profit Cuban Museum Inc. Partner of the Foundation for Human Rights in Cuba on its Castro Power Deck project.

f: Florida non-profit run by a volunteer board that says donations and volunteers maintain the building. State of Florida grants of $2.8 million paid for the restoration reopened in 1992.
w: Founded in 1871 by Cuban exiles. Cuba's government gave $80,000 for the 1920s rebuilding and paid a teacher's salary until 1959.
x: Files a full Form 990 (2019 is the latest on ProPublica) and lists its board on its site.
2019 revenue $144,130: contributions $30,081, rental income $29,698, other $84,341; expenses $261,767 (Form 990, ProPublica).
Rental income and contributions (2019: $29,698 and $30,081 of $144,130). State of Florida grants of $2.8 million paid for the restoration reopened in 1992.
Operated by the Florida non-profit Instituto Patriótico y Docente San Carlos Inc. Houses its own museum, library, theatre, school and art gallery.

f: Independent art institute founded in 2015 and set up by a crowdfunding campaign of 915 backers. In 2024 its whole income, $95,283, came from Estudio Bruguera, the founder's studio.
w: Cuban authorities detained founder Tania Bruguera in December 2014 and January 2015; INSTAR says the street outside was drilled during its 2015 reading.
x: Publishes yearly finance reports (2016 to 2024) with income and spending lines, a named donor list and a statement of its funding principles.
2024 income $95,283 and spending $95,283; the income was a donation from Estudio Bruguera (INSTAR 2024 finance report).

Estudio Bruguera, the founder's studio, gave all income in 2021, 2023 and 2024 and $159,558 of $232,171 in 2022. The other $72,613 in 2022 backed documenta fifteen: Fundación Familia Pérez, Prince Claus Foundation, Lumbung, Allianz Foundation and merchandise sales.

Member of the CIVICUS network since 2020 and part of documenta fifteen's lumbung network. Allies named on its site include the 27N platform, PEN America's Artists at Risk Connection, GAPAC, Rialta and Haus der Kulturen der Welt.

f: Non-profit educational institution founded in 1972 that runs the Cuban Art Space gallery. Its 2024 revenue was $296,120, of which $194,216 was contributions and $86,374 program services (Form 990).
w: Founded in 1972 to counter US policy toward Cuba. A bomb wrecked its New York premises on 28 March 1973; its letter named no perpetrator.
x: Files a full Form 990 (2024 filed 18 November 2025, on ProPublica) that lists its officers.
2024 revenue $296,120: contributions $194,216, program services $86,374, inventory sales $14,270; expenses $378,092 (Form 990, ProPublica).
Contributions (about 66 percent of 2024 revenue: $194,216 of $296,120), program income ($86,374) and inventory sales ($14,270).
A New York non-profit that runs the Cuban Art Space inside the Center, a collection of over 10,000 posters, prints and photographs. It also organises travel to Cuba.

f: A building of 1860 to 1868 on Parque Calixto García houses Holguín's state provincial history museum, whose heritage centre lists six rooms; EcuRed says one is mounted.
w: National Monument since 10 October 1978. Spanish Wikipedia dates the museum to 1980, EcuRed to 25 July 1976.
x: The Holguín heritage centre's own site describes the museum and its halls; it links no accounts or budget.
Centro Provincial de Patrimonio Cultural de Holguín, which heads a Ministry of Culture system of 25 museums and 11 extensions that includes this one (Cuban state).
A museum of the Centro Provincial de Patrimonio Cultural de Holguín, which heads a system of 25 museums and 11 extensions subordinate to the Ministry of Culture (the centre's own site, 2023).

n: Museo Provincial de Pinar del Río
f: State provincial history museum in a building that housed the provincial government from 1892 to 1959. It belongs to the Pinar del Río provincial heritage centre.
w: Opened with one room on 14 December 1979 and the rest in 1981. Rooms cover archaeology, history, decorative arts and local musicians.
x: Centro Provincial de Patrimonio Cultural Pinar del Río, whose museum network includes it (EcuRed), within the Ministry of Culture (Cuban state).
Part of the museum network of the Centro Provincial de Patrimonio Cultural Pinar del Río (EcuRed), within the Consejo Nacional de Patrimonio Cultural system.

n: Museo Provincial de Granma Manuel Muñoz Cedeño
f: Bayamo's provincial museum opened on 19 October 1982 as the Museo Histórico de Bayamo, in the city's historic centre. It belongs to the Centro Provincial de Patrimonio Cultural en Granma.
w: Armando Hart, then minister of culture, attended the opening. Bayamo's historic centre has been a National Monument since 1935, ratified in 1978.
x: Centro Provincial de Patrimonio Cultural en Granma, within the Ministry of Culture's heritage system (Cuban state; Radio Bayamo, 2025).

A provincial museum in the Consejo Nacional de Patrimonio Cultural system (Ministry of Culture). The Centro Provincial de Patrimonio Cultural en Granma held its yearly review assembly there (Radio Bayamo, 23 December 2025).
